web_evidence.title: Jaws | Penguin Random House Retail
web_evidence.note: The publisher's sustained chapter-one excerpt narrates the fish and the woman externally in third person, including access to their sensations and internal states.

web_evidence.title: 2016 MCAS English Language Arts: excerpts from Jaws and Swimming with Nightmares
web_evidence.note: This officially reproduced, permission-cleared interior excerpt sustains third-person narration through Hooper's cage dive and shifts between Hooper, Brody, Quint, and the fish.

web_evidence.title: Jaws and the Nature of Evil: An Examination of Peter Benchley's Jaws as a Work of Gothic Fiction
web_evidence.note: The University of Oregon thesis explicitly identifies the narration entering Ellen's perceptions as third-person limited and analyzes comparable perspective shifts elsewhere in the novel.

web_evidence.title: Jaws by Peter Benchley: A Book Review
web_evidence.note: The completed-book review explicitly describes shifts between third-person limited and omniscient narration; these are focalization changes within third person, not changes of grammatical person.

person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and consistently uses third person, with focalization moving among the shark, Brody, Ellen, Hooper, and attack victims. Numerous event quotes independently corroborate the publisher's sustained third-person opening and the permission-cleared interior Hooper excerpt; scholarly analysis explicitly identifies Ellen's passages as third-person limited. First- and second-person forms in the inputs belong to dialogue, direct thought, an embedded newspaper editorial, gnomic material, or later authorial paratext, not autonomous base sections. q01967 appears narratorial despite its dialogue bucket, while q01982 and q01991 remain too clipped for local attribution. No credible source indicates person alternation; the remaining uncertainty concerns only those individual quote boundaries, not the book-level label.
